arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Kneedler argued Section 1395hh did not require notice-and-comment rulemaking.
He stated the agency only shared a calculation component with contractors.
Mr. Shah argued the agency reduced hospital payment rights by billions of dollars.
He claimed the agency made a legal determination without proper procedure.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The dispute centers on how Medicare calculates hospital reimbursement. Hospitals claim the agency changed payment rules without proper notice. The government argues this was an internal calculation, not a rule.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the boundary between agency rules and internal calculations. It determines when hospitals must receive formal notice before payment changes. The outcome shapes administrative agency power over healthcare funding.
